correctness.rationale: Forbidden length-one overlaps normalize all nonempty binary codes to 7-bit prefix masks starting zero and 7-bit suffix masks ending one. For n>=14, all middle 2^(n-14) blocks are independent of forbidden overlap checks of lengths <=7. The common-neighbor maps form a Galois connection; closure retains the neighbor set, so maximizing subsets may be taken closed. Exact complete NextClosure traversal of the fully reconstructed 64x64 relation has 1,944 closed prefix sets and maximum |X|*|N(X)|=744. Dual 1,944-concept traversal and published cutoff-five/six baseline tests independently cross-check indexing and the enumeration; direct exhaustive search of 2^16 masks at cutoff five corroborates. P={p_0,...,p_23} has exactly 31 compatible suffixes, achieving 744. verify.py is self-contained and recomputed from its embedded bytes.

value.rationale: This closes the first fixed cutoff not resolved in the 2022 restricted-overlap code paper: its proof of exact binary maxima ends at k=6 and it explicitly regards k>=7 brute search as infeasible. Establishing the sharp k=7 coefficient 744, not merely reproducing a lower-bound witness, quantifies the attainable cardinality for every block length n>=14. The natural parameter is a published synchronization-code extremal invariant with motivation independent of enumeration.
